profiles.name: EDTF Level 0
profiles.description: Extended Date/Time Format Level 0 as defined in Annex A of ISO 8601-2 (Library of Congress EDTF specification). EDTF Level 0 is a subset of ISO 8601-1 supporting only extended format representations with restricted granularity options.

additional_requirements.statement: Only extended format representations shall be used. Basic format representations (without delimiters) are not permitted.
Calendar year representations shall be exactly four digits. Year expansion (agreed number of digits) and reduced precision below day in intervals are not permitted.
The time designator "T" shall be mandatory between the date and time components in date-and-time representations.
Time-of-day representations shall include at least hours and minutes (hh:mm minimum). Representations with hour-only precision are not permitted.
The hour value 24 is not allowed. Midnight shall be represented as 00:00 of the following day.
UTC offset shall be represented either as "Z" or as a numeric offset with both hours and minutes (±hh:mm). Offset without minutes (±hh) is not permitted.

profiles.name: EDTF Level 1
profiles.description: Extended Date/Time Format Level 1 as defined in Annex A of ISO 8601-2 (Library of Congress EDTF specification). EDTF Level 1 extends Level 0 with uncertain/approximate qualification, unspecified digits, and season representations drawn from ISO 8601-2.

additional_requirements.statement: Only extended format representations shall be used. Basic format representations (without delimiters) are not permitted.
Calendar year representations shall be exactly four digits.
The time designator "T" shall be mandatory between the date and time components in date-and-time representations.
Time-of-day representations shall include at least hours and minutes (hh:mm minimum).
The hour value 24 is not allowed.
UTC offset shall be represented either as "Z" or as a numeric offset with both hours and minutes (±hh:mm).

The qualification markers "?" (uncertain) and "~" (approximate) may be appended to a date or date component value. The marker "?" indicates uncertainty about the value; the marker "~" indicates the value is approximate.

Unspecified digits shall be represented by "X" characters. For a two-digit field (month or day), exactly two "X" characters ("XX") shall be used to indicate the entire field is unspecified. A single "X" in a two-digit field is not permitted.
Seasons shall be represented using the values 21 (Spring), 22 (Summer), 23 (Autumn/Fall), 24 (Winter) appended to a year with hyphen separator (e.g. 2001-21 for Spring 2001).

profiles.name: EDTF Level 2
profiles.description: Extended Date/Time Format Level 2 as defined in Annex A of ISO 8601-2 (Library of Congress EDTF specification). EDTF Level 2 extends Level 1 with partial uncertain/approximate qualification, sets and ranges, extended time intervals, and exponential values.

additional_requirements.statement: Only extended format representations shall be used. Basic format representations (without delimiters) are not permitted.
Calendar year representations shall be exactly four digits.
The time designator "T" shall be mandatory between the date and time components in date-and-time representations.
Time-of-day representations shall include at least hours and minutes (hh:mm minimum).
The hour value 24 is not allowed.
UTC offset shall be represented either as "Z" or as a numeric offset with both hours and minutes (±hh:mm).
The qualification markers "?" (uncertain) and "~" (approximate) may be appended to a date or date component value.
Unspecified digits shall be represented by "X" characters. For a two-digit field, exactly "XX" shall be used.
Seasons shall be represented using the values 21 (Spring), 22 (Summer), 23 (Autumn/Fall), 24 (Winter).
Qualification markers may be applied to individual components within a date by enclosing the qualified component in parentheses, e.g. "2004-(06)?-11" indicates uncertainty only about the month.
Unspecified digits ("XX") may be applied independently to the month or day field, e.g. "2018-XX-03" (month unspecified, day known) or "2018-03-XX" (day unspecified, month known).

Sets and ranges shall use square brackets for inclusive ranges ("[..]") and curly braces for enumerated sets ("{},"). Open-ended ranges are indicated by omitting the start or end value within brackets, e.g. "[..1760]" or "[1760..]".
Year values may use exponential notation in the form of "yEy" where E is a signed or unsigned integer exponent, e.g. "y-5E7" represents the year -50000000.

profiles.name: ISO 8601-1 Basic Format
profiles.description: Profile of ISO 8601-1 covering basic format representations only (without hyphens, colons, or other delimiters between numeric components). Basic format uses compact representations suitable for systems with bandwidth or storage constraints. Only the time designator "T", zone designator "Z", and sign characters may appear as non-numeric separators.

additional_requirements.statement: Date and time representations shall use basic format without hyphens, colons, or other delimiter characters between numeric components. Only the time designator "T", zone designator "Z", and sign characters (±) may appear as non-numeric characters.
Calendar date shall be represented as YYYYMMDD (e.g. 19850412).
Ordinal date shall be represented as YYYYDDD (e.g. 1985102).
Week date shall be represented as YYYYWwwD (e.g. 1985W155).
Time of day shall be represented as hhmmss or hhmm (e.g. 232050).
UTC offset in basic format shall use ±hhmm or Z (e.g. +0200).

profiles.name: ISO 8601-1 Complete
profiles.description: Profile covering all conformance classes defined in ISO 8601-1 (Date and time — Representations for information interchange — Part 1: Basic rules).

profiles.name: ISO 8601-1 Core
profiles.description: Core profile covering the commonly supported subset of ISO 8601-1: extended-format calendar dates (YYYY-MM-DD, YYYY-MM, YYYY), time of day (hh:mm:ss, hh:mm), and date-time combinations (YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ, etc.). This profile represents what virtually every standard library date/time parser handles well. Excludes basic format, week/ordinal dates, expanded years, durations, intervals, and edge-case fundamentals (time-shift as standalone concept, expansion, leading-zeros validation).

profiles.name: ISO 8601-2 Complete
profiles.description: Profile covering all conformance classes defined in both ISO 8601-1 (Basic rules) and ISO 8601-2 (Extensions).

profiles.name: RFC 3339
profiles.description: Profile of ISO 8601-1 for Internet date/time formats as defined in RFC 3339. This profile restricts ISO 8601 to extended format only, requires full date (YYYY-MM-DD), mandates seconds in time representations, requires UTC offset, disallows hour 24, permits lowercase t/z, and accommodates leap seconds (second value 60).

additional_requirements.statement: Only extended format representations shall be used. Basic format representations (without hyphens or colons as delimiters) are not permitted.

The time designator between the date and time components shall be "T" or "t". Applications that generate this format SHOULD use uppercase "T". Parsers SHALL accept both uppercase "T" and lowercase "t".
Every date-time representation shall include either the UTC designator "Z" (or "z") or a numeric UTC offset (±hh:mm). Representations without a UTC offset are not permitted.
The hour value 24 is not allowed. Midnight shall be represented as 00:00:00 of the following day.
Date representations shall be complete calendar dates (YYYY-MM-DD) only. Reduced precision forms (YYYY or YYYY-MM) are not permitted as standalone values.

Time representations shall include seconds (hh:mm:ss). Fractional seconds (hh:mm:ss.s) are optional but the integer seconds field is mandatory. Representations with only hours and minutes (hh:mm) are not permitted.
Numeric UTC offsets shall include both hours and minutes (±hh:mm). Offset representations without minutes (±hh) are not permitted.
The second value 60 is permitted to represent a positive leap second. When a leap second occurs, the second field may contain the value "60" in place of the normal maximum of "59".

The UTC offset "-00:00" indicates that the date-time is in UTC but the local time zone relationship is unknown. This differs from "+00:00" which indicates UTC with a known zero offset. Both "-00:00" and "+00:00" are valid representations.
The UTC designator "Z" may alternatively be lowercase "z". Applications that generate this format SHOULD use uppercase "Z". Parsers SHALL accept both uppercase "Z" and lowercase "z".

profiles.name: W3C Date and Time Formats
profiles.description: Profile of ISO 8601-1 for date and time formats as defined in the W3C NOTE-datetime. This profile defines six permitted granularity levels using extended format only. Year is always four digits, hour is 00–23, and time zone designator is required when time is present.

additional_requirements.statement: Only extended format representations shall be used. Basic format representations (without hyphens or colons as delimiters) are not permitted.
Only the following six forms are permitted: YYYY, YYYY-MM, YYYY-MM-DD, YYYY-MM-DDThh:mmTZD, YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssTZD, YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.sTZD. No other forms are permitted.
When time is present, the time zone designator (TZD) shall be either "Z" (for UTC) or a numeric offset in the form ±hh:mm. Time representations without a time zone designator are not permitted.
The time designator between the date and time components shall be "T" (uppercase or lowercase).
Fractional seconds, when present, shall consist of a decimal point followed by one or more digits.
Year shall be represented as exactly four digits. Two-digit year representations are not permitted. This avoids the ambiguity of two-digit century representations.
Hour values shall be in the range 00 through 23. The 12-hour notation with am/pm is not permitted.

requirements.statement: Time of day is expressed using a 24-hour clock. A clock hour is identified by a two-digit ordinal number from '00' to '23'. A clock minute from '00' to '59'. A clock second from '00' to '60' (60 accommodates leap seconds).
Adding two durations produces a new duration whose time scale components are the arithmetic sums of the corresponding input components.
A date and time expression can be reduced to canonical form with no overflow and minimal underflow.
In composite duration arithmetic, adding two durations yields a new duration with component-wise sums of the corresponding fields.
Some pairs of time scale components convert unambiguously while others do not, establishing conversion boundaries between units.
A date and time expression may be shifted by a duration through addition: date = dateA + durationB.
When the duration is in precedence representation, evaluation proceeds from the leftmost durational unit to the rightmost.
A duration may be scaled by a scalar multiplier, producing a new duration.
Component values exceeding their valid range indicate overflow (positive excess) or underflow (negative excess).
In precedence duration arithmetic, adding two durations concatenates the durational units without computing component-level sums.
Subtracting a duration is equivalent to adding the negation of that duration.
Calendar date shall be represented as YYYYMMDD (e.g. 19850412).
UTC offset in basic format shall use ±hhmm or Z (e.g. +0200).
Ordinal date shall be represented as YYYYDDD (e.g. 1985102).
Time of day shall be represented as hhmmss or hhmm (e.g. 232050).
Week date shall be represented as YYYYWwwD (e.g. 1985W155).

Date and time representations shall use basic format without hyphens, colons, or other delimiter characters between numeric components. Only the time designator "T", zone designator "Z", and sign characters (±) may appear as non-numeric characters.
A complete calendar date in basic format encodes the year, month, and day as contiguous digit fields without separators: [year][month][day].
An expanded calendar century in basic format encodes a signed expanded century field: [±][cent(expanded)].
An expanded calendar decade in basic format encodes a signed expanded decade field: [±][dec(expanded)].
An expanded calendar day in basic format encodes a signed expanded year field with month and day: [±][year(expanded)][month][day].
An expanded calendar year in basic format encodes a signed expanded year without separators: [±][year(expanded)].
An expanded calendar day in extended format encodes a signed expanded year with hyphen-separated month and day: [±][year(expanded)]["-"][month]["-"][day].
An expanded calendar month in extended format encodes a signed expanded year with hyphen separator and month: [±][year(expanded)]["-"][month].
A complete calendar date in extended format encodes the year, month, and day with hyphen separators: [year]["-"][month]["-"][day].
A calendar century with reduced precision is expressed in basic format as [cent] (two digits).
A calendar decade with reduced precision is expressed in basic format as [dec] (three digits).
A calendar month with reduced precision (day omitted) in extended format uses only year and month with hyphen separator: [year]["-"][month].
A calendar year with reduced precision (month and day omitted) is expressed in basic format as [year].
Each Gregorian calendar century is identified by a 2-digit ordinal number beginning with '00', for century zero, through '99'. The century is represented in implied form as [YY].

The character set used in ISO 8601 representations shall be limited to digits 0 through 9, and the separator and designator characters hyphen-minus (-), colon (:), letter T, letter W, letter P, letter R, letter Z, plus sign (+), and solidus (/).
A calendar date combined with local time in basic format concatenates the date and time fields with a time designator: [date]["T"][time].
A calendar date combined with time and UTC offset in basic format appends the offset after the time: [date]["T"][time][shift] or [date]["T"][time][shiftH].
A calendar date combined with UTC time in basic format appends the UTC designator after the time: [date]["T"][time]["Z"].
A calendar date combined with local time in extended format uses hyphen separators in the date and colon separators in the time: [dateX]["T"][timeX].
A calendar date combined with time and UTC offset in extended format appends the offset: [dateX]["T"][timeX][shiftX] or [dateX]["T"][timeX][shiftH].
A calendar date combined with UTC time in extended format appends the UTC designator: [dateX]["T"][timeX]["Z"].
An ordinal date combined with local time in basic format concatenates the date and time with a time designator: [odate]["T"][time].
An ordinal date combined with time and UTC offset in basic format appends the offset: [odate]["T"][time][shift] or [odate]["T"][time][shiftH].
An ordinal date combined with UTC time in basic format appends the UTC designator: [odate]["T"][time]["Z"].
An ordinal date combined with local time in extended format uses hyphen and colon separators: [odateX]["T"][timeX].
An ordinal date combined with time and UTC offset in extended format appends the offset: [odateX]["T"][timeX][shiftX] or [odateX]["T"][timeX][shiftH].
An ordinal date combined with UTC time in extended format appends the UTC designator: [odateX]["T"][timeX]["Z"].

A date expression followed by ["T"] may include a time component with reduced precision (omitting seconds or minutes). The entire expression must use either basic format or extended format consistently.
A week date combined with local time in basic format concatenates the date and time with a time designator: [wdate]["T"][time].
A week date combined with time and UTC offset in basic format appends the offset: [wdate]["T"][time][shift] or [wdate]["T"][time][shiftH].
A week date combined with UTC time in basic format appends the UTC designator: [wdate]["T"][time]["Z"].
A week date combined with local time in extended format uses hyphen and colon separators: [wdateX]["T"][timeX].
A week date combined with time and UTC offset in extended format appends the offset: [wdateX]["T"][timeX][shiftX] or [wdateX]["T"][timeX][shiftH].
A week date combined with UTC time in extended format appends the UTC designator: [wdateX]["T"][timeX]["Z"].
The calendar day of week is represented by a single digit ordinal number from '1' (Monday) through '7' (Sunday).
The calendar day of year is represented by a three-digit ordinal number from '001' (January 1) through '365' (common year) or '366' (leap year).

Calendar months shall have the following number of days: January 31, February 28 (29 in leap years), March 31, April 30, May 31, June 30, July 31, August 31, September 30, October 31, November 30, December 31.
Each Gregorian calendar decade is identified by a 3-digit ordinal number beginning with '000', for decade zero, through '999'. The decade is represented in implied form as [YYY].
The decreasing order of time scale components, left-to-right, is common to all date and time representations.
By mutual agreement, a duration may use the alternative form with calendar date in basic format: ["P"][date]["T"][time].
By mutual agreement, a duration may use the alternative form with calendar date in extended format: ["P"][dateX]["T"][timeX].
By mutual agreement, a duration may use the alternative form with ordinal date in basic format: ["P"][odate]["T"][time].
By mutual agreement, a duration may use the alternative form with ordinal date in extended format: ["P"][odateX]["T"][timeX].
A complete duration expression uses the period designator followed by date and time unit groups: ["P"][i]["Y"][i]["M"][i]["D"]["T"][i]["H"][i]["M"][i]["S"], where each [i] is a positive integer.
A duration may also be expressed using only weeks: ["P"][i]["W"]. Week-based and date-time-based expressions are mutually exclusive within a single duration.
The lowest-order component may include a decimal fraction, separated from the integer part by a decimal sign (period or comma) with at least one fractional digit.
Components with a value of zero may be omitted along with their designator, provided at least one component with its designator remains present.
The time designator ["T"] separates date-unit components from time-unit components within a duration. If no time components are present, the time designator is omitted.
Only extended format representations shall be used. Basic format representations (without delimiters) are not permitted.
Calendar year representations shall be exactly four digits. Year expansion (agreed number of digits) and reduced precision below day in intervals are not permitted.
The time designator "T" shall be mandatory between the date and time components in date-and-time representations.
The hour value 24 is not allowed. Midnight shall be represented as 00:00 of the following day.
UTC offset shall be represented either as "Z" or as a numeric offset with both hours and minutes (±hh:mm). Offset without minutes (±hh) is not permitted.
Time-of-day representations shall include at least hours and minutes (hh:mm minimum). Representations with hour-only precision are not permitted.
Only extended format representations shall be used. Basic format representations (without delimiters) are not permitted.
Calendar year representations shall be exactly four digits.
The time designator "T" shall be mandatory between the date and time components in date-and-time representations.
The hour value 24 is not allowed.
UTC offset shall be represented either as "Z" or as a numeric offset with both hours and minutes (±hh:mm).

The qualification markers "?" (uncertain) and "~" (approximate) may be appended to a date or date component value. The marker "?" indicates uncertainty about the value; the marker "~" indicates the value is approximate.
Seasons shall be represented using the values 21 (Spring), 22 (Summer), 23 (Autumn/Fall), 24 (Winter) appended to a year with hyphen separator (e.g. 2001-21 for Spring 2001).
Time-of-day representations shall include at least hours and minutes (hh:mm minimum).

Unspecified digits shall be represented by "X" characters. For a two-digit field (month or day), exactly two "X" characters ("XX") shall be used to indicate the entire field is unspecified. A single "X" in a two-digit field is not permitted.
Year values may use exponential notation in the form of "yEy" where E is a signed or unsigned integer exponent, e.g. "y-5E7" represents the year -50000000.
Only extended format representations shall be used. Basic format representations (without delimiters) are not permitted.
Calendar year representations shall be exactly four digits.
The time designator "T" shall be mandatory between the date and time components in date-and-time representations.
The hour value 24 is not allowed.
UTC offset shall be represented either as "Z" or as a numeric offset with both hours and minutes (±hh:mm).
Qualification markers may be applied to individual components within a date by enclosing the qualified component in parentheses, e.g. "2004-(06)?-11" indicates uncertainty only about the month.
Unspecified digits ("XX") may be applied independently to the month or day field, e.g. "2018-XX-03" (month unspecified, day known) or "2018-03-XX" (day unspecified, month known).
The qualification markers "?" (uncertain) and "~" (approximate) may be appended to a date or date component value.
Seasons shall be represented using the values 21 (Spring), 22 (Summer), 23 (Autumn/Fall), 24 (Winter).

Sets and ranges shall use square brackets for inclusive ranges ("[..]") and curly braces for enumerated sets ("{},"). Open-ended ranges are indicated by omitting the start or end value within brackets, e.g. "[..1760]" or "[1760..]".
Time-of-day representations shall include at least hours and minutes (hh:mm minimum).
Unspecified digits shall be represented by "X" characters. For a two-digit field, exactly "XX" shall be used.

By mutual agreement of the communicating partners, it is permitted to expand the component identifying the calendar year, which is otherwise limited to four digits. This enables reference to dates where the calendar year identifier exceeds four digits.

requirements.category: Explicit representation for date and time
requirements.statement: The century in explicit form encodes the value with the C designator: [i]["C"].

requirements.category: Explicit representation for date and time
requirements.statement: The calendar day of week in explicit form encodes the value with the K designator: [i]["K"].

requirements.category: Explicit representation for date and time
requirements.statement: The calendar day of year in explicit form encodes the value with the O designator: [i]["O"].

requirements.category: Explicit representation for date and time
requirements.statement: The decade in explicit form encodes the value with the J designator: [i]["J"].

requirements.category: Explicit representation for date and time
requirements.statement: The beginning of the day in explicit form is encoded as T0H0M0S. Zero-valued components may be omitted per the omission rules.

requirements.category: Explicit representation for date and time
requirements.statement: A calendar date in explicit form encodes the year, month, and day with their respective designator symbols: [yearE][monthE][dayE].

requirements.category: Explicit representation for date and time
requirements.statement: A century in explicit form encodes the century value with its designator symbol: [centE].

requirements.category: Explicit representation for date and time
requirements.statement: A date with a time shift in explicit form combines the date and shift: [dateE][shiftE].

requirements.category: Explicit representation for date and time
requirements.statement: A date and time in explicit form combines the date and time expressions: [dateE][timeE], denoted as [datetimeE].

requirements.category: Explicit representation for date and time
requirements.statement: A date and time with a time shift in explicit form combines date, time, and shift: [dateE][timeE][shiftE].

requirements.category: Explicit representation for date and time
requirements.statement: A decade in explicit form encodes the decade value with its designator symbol: [decE].

requirements.category: Explicit representation for date and time
requirements.statement: Explicit form expressions may include a decimal fraction on the hour, minute, or second component.

requirements.category: Explicit representation for date and time
requirements.statement: Local time of day in explicit form encodes the time designator followed by hour, minute, and second with designator symbols: ["T"][hourE][minE][secE], denoted as [timeE].

requirements.category: Explicit representation for date and time
requirements.statement: A time scale component whose value is zero may be omitted along with its designator, except when omission would alter the precision indication.

requirements.category: Explicit representation for date and time
requirements.statement: An ordinal date in explicit form encodes the year and day-of-year with their respective designator symbols: [yearE][dayoE].

requirements.category: Explicit representation for date and time
requirements.statement: The lowest-order time scale component present in an explicit date-time expression determines the precision of that expression.

requirements.category: Explicit representation for date and time
requirements.statement: A recurring time interval in explicit form prefixes the interval with the recurrence designator: ["R"][n]["/"][timeIntervalE].

requirements.category: Explicit representation for date and time
requirements.statement: Higher-order time scale components may be omitted from the end of an explicit time interval, provided the expression remains unambiguous.

requirements.category: Explicit representation for date and time
requirements.statement: A time interval in explicit form with duration and end: [duration]["/"][dtE].

requirements.category: Explicit representation for date and time
requirements.statement: A time shift specified in the start component of an explicit interval is assumed to apply to the end component, unless the end provides its own shift.

requirements.category: Explicit representation for date and time
requirements.statement: A time interval in explicit form with start and duration: [dtE]["/"][duration].

requirements.category: Explicit representation for date and time
requirements.statement: A time interval in explicit form with start and end date: [dtE]["/"][dtE].

requirements.category: Explicit representation for date and time
requirements.statement: The explicit time form [timeE] supports reduced precision by including only [hourE] or [hourE] and [minE], with trailing components omitted.

requirements.category: Explicit representation for date and time
requirements.statement: A time shift in explicit form is represented as ["Z"] or ["-"][timeUnits], denoted as [shiftE].

requirements.category: Explicit representation for date and time
requirements.statement: A time of day with a time shift in explicit form combines the time and shift: [timeE][shiftE].

requirements.category: Explicit representation for date and time
requirements.statement: Leading zeros may be prepended to values in explicit form time scale components.

requirements.category: Explicit representation for date and time
requirements.statement: A week date in explicit form encodes the year, week number, and day of week with their respective designator symbols: [yearE][weekE][daykE].

requirements.category: Exponential values for time scale components
requirements.statement: An exponential calendar year in explicit form replaces the integer placeholder with an exponential value, producing the year designator: [significand]["E"][exponent]["Y"].

requirements.category: Exponential values for time scale components
requirements.statement: An exponential calendar year with letter prefix combines the Y designator with a signed integer and exponent: ["Y"][negi]["E"][i].

requirements.category: Exponential values for time scale components
requirements.statement: An exponential value encodes a significand and exponent: [significand]["E"][exponent], where the significand is a positive or negative integer and the exponent is a positive integer power of 10.

requirements.category: Exponential values for time scale components
requirements.statement: Any time scale component that accepts unbounded integers or describes a duration may substitute the integer placeholder [i] with an exponential value [exp].
"Before" and "after" boundaries with qualified time scale components use double-dot notation within time interval expressions.
A time interval with an open (continuing) end encodes the start followed by a solidus and double-dot: [intexpr]["/"][".."].
A time interval with an open (unbounded earlier) start encodes a double-dot followed by a solidus and the end: [".."]["/"][intexpr].
Start and end dates within a time interval may carry uncertainty and approximation qualification symbols.
Individual portions of the start and/or end dates in a time interval may be independently qualified.
Start and end dates may combine uncertainty/approximation qualification, unspecified digits, and open or unknown boundary notations within a single time interval.
A time interval with an unknown end encodes the start followed by a trailing solidus: [intexpr]["/"].
A time interval with an unknown start encodes a leading solidus followed by the end: ["/"][intexpr].
Portions of the start or end date in a time interval may use the "X" unspecified-digit notation.

The Gregorian calendar governs the identification of calendar days. This calendar structures time as a continuous sequence of calendar years, with common years containing 365 days and leap years containing 366 days. Each calendar year comprises 12 consecutive calendar months.
Grouped time scale units may replace any time scale unit in a date or time expression, provided the resulting expression remains valid.
Components appearing to the right of a grouped time scale unit describe instances within that grouped unit.
Lower-order component values must remain within the bounds established by the grouped time scale unit definition.
A grouped time scale unit expression can be converted into an equivalent time interval using basic time scale units.
An expression using grouped time scale units may include a time shift: [groupDateTime][shiftE].
When a grouped unit does not evenly divide the original component, the final unit spans only the remaining bounded duration.
A grouped time scale unit is enclosed by the G prefix and U suffix, with one or more positive duration components in between: ["G"][durationUnits]["U"].
The value of a grouped unit combines a coefficient with the grouped unit definition: [i][groupUnit], where [i] selects the specific sub-unit.

In a start/end interval, higher-order time scale components may be omitted from the end expression when the result remains unambiguous. The omitted components inherit their values from the start expression.
A time interval specified by duration and end in basic format encodes a duration followed by a solidus and the end date-time: [duration]["/"][date]["T"][time].
A time interval specified by duration and end in extended format encodes a duration followed by a solidus and the end date-time: [duration]["/"][dateX]["T"][timeX].
A time interval specified by start and duration in basic format encodes the start date-time followed by a solidus and a duration: [date]["T"][time]["/"][duration].
A time interval specified by start and duration in extended format encodes the start date-time followed by a solidus and a duration: [dateX]["T"][timeX]["/"][duration].
A time interval specified by start and end in basic format concatenates two date-time expressions with a solidus separator: [date]["T"][time]["/"][date]["T"][time].
A time interval specified by start and end in extended format concatenates two extended date-time expressions with a solidus separator: [dateX]["T"][timeX]["/"][dateX]["T"][timeX].
A UTC offset provided with the component before the solidus is assumed to apply to the component after the solidus, unless the latter provides its own offset.
If a time scale component in an implied representation has a fixed length, leading zeros shall be used as required.

A calendar year is a leap year if it is divisible by 4, except that years divisible by 100 are not leap years unless they are also divisible by 400. A leap year has 366 days with February having 29 days; a common year has 365 days with February having 28 days.
Each calendar month within its calendar year is identified by a two-digit ordinal number from '01' for January to '12' for December.

requirements.category: Negative values for time scale components
requirements.statement: The calendar century in explicit form permits negative values by prefixing a minus sign: [!]["-"][centE].

requirements.category: Negative values for time scale components
requirements.statement: The calendar century in implicit form permits negative values by prefixing a minus sign: [!]["-"][cent].

requirements.category: Negative values for time scale components
requirements.statement: The calendar day of month in explicit form permits negative values: [!]["-"][dayE]. A negative day number counts in reverse from the end of the month.

requirements.category: Negative values for time scale components
requirements.statement: The calendar day of year in explicit form permits negative values: [!]["-"][dayoE]. A negative day-of-year counts in reverse from the end of the year.

requirements.category: Negative values for time scale components
requirements.statement: The calendar decade in explicit form permits negative values by prefixing a minus sign: [!]["-"][decE].

requirements.category: Negative values for time scale components
requirements.statement: The calendar decade in implicit form permits negative values by prefixing a minus sign: [!]["-"][dec].

requirements.category: Negative values for time scale components
requirements.statement: A negative duration prefixes the entire positive duration with a minus sign: [!]["-"][positiveDuration]. All individual time scale components within the duration remain positive.

requirements.category: Negative values for time scale components
requirements.statement: The calendar week of year in explicit form permits negative values: [!]["-"][weekE]. A negative week number counts in reverse from the end of the year.

requirements.category: Negative values for time scale components
requirements.statement: A calendar year preceding year one is represented in explicit form with a B suffix: [yearE]["B"].

requirements.category: Negative values for time scale components
requirements.statement: The calendar year in explicit form permits negative values by prefixing a minus sign: [!]["-"][yearE].

requirements.category: Negative values for time scale components
requirements.statement: The calendar year in implicit form permits negative values by prefixing a minus sign: [!]["-"][year].
A complete ordinal date in basic format encodes the year and day-of-year as contiguous digit fields: [year][dayo].
An expanded ordinal date in basic format encodes a signed expanded year and day-of-year: [±][year(expanded)][dayo].
An expanded ordinal date in extended format encodes a signed expanded year and day-of-year with a hyphen separator: [±][year(expanded)]["-"][dayo].
A complete ordinal date in extended format encodes the year and day-of-year with a hyphen separator: [year]["-"][dayo].
A fully qualified calendar date places the qualifier at the end of the expression, applying to the entire date in both implicit and explicit formats.
Group qualification covering day, month, and year simultaneously places the qualifier [Q] after the day component.
Group qualification covering month and year places the qualifier [Q] after the month component.
Group qualification covering only the year places the qualifier [Q] after the year component.
Individual qualification of calendar date components applies a separate qualifier symbol to each targeted component.
Century qualification in explicit form: [i][!][Q]["C"].
Century qualification in implicit form: [!][Q][YY].
Complete qualification applies to the entire date-time expression by placing the qualification symbol at the rightmost end.
The qualification mechanism extends to combined date and time expressions, qualifying the relevant time scale components within the expression.
Calendar day of month qualification in explicit form: [i][!][Q]["D"].
Calendar day of month qualification in implicit form: [!][Q][DD].
Calendar day of week qualification in explicit form: [i][!][Q]["K"].
Calendar day of week qualification in implicit form: [!][Q][K].
Calendar day of year qualification in explicit form: [i][!][Q]["O"].
Calendar day of year qualification in implicit form: [!][Q][OOO].
Decade qualification in explicit form: [i][!][Q]["J"].
Decade qualification in implicit form: [!][Q][YYY].
In explicit form, the qualifier appears between the value and its designator symbol: [i][!][Q][symbol(c)].
Group qualification applies the qualifier to a component and all components to its left. The qualifier appears immediately to the right of the targeted component.
Clock hour qualification in explicit form: [i][!][Q]["H"].
Clock hour qualification in implicit form: [!][Q][hh].
In implicit form, a qualification marker precedes the component it modifies: [!][Q][c], where [Q] is one of the qualifying symbols ("?", "~", or "%").
Individual qualification targets a single component. In implicit form the qualifier precedes the component; in explicit form it appears between the value and the designator.
Clock minute qualification in explicit form: [i][!][Q]["M"].
Clock minute qualification in implicit form: [!][Q][mm].
Calendar month qualification in explicit form: [i][!][Q]["M"].
Calendar month qualification in implicit form: [!][Q][MM].
Clock second qualification in explicit form: [i][!][Q]["S"].
Clock second qualification in implicit form: [!][Q][ss].
Calendar week qualification in explicit form: [i][!][Q]["W"].
Calendar week qualification in implicit form: [!][Q]["W"][WW].
Calendar year qualification in explicit form places the qualifier before the year designator: [i][!][Q]["Y"].
Calendar year qualification in implicit form places the qualifier before the year field: [!][Q][YYYY].
Every recurring time interval begins with the recurrence designator ["R"], followed without spaces by an optional recurrence count [n], then a solidus ["/"] — also without intervening spaces.
A recurring time interval with duration and end in basic format: ["R"][n]["/"][duration]["/"][date]["T"][time].
A recurring time interval with duration and end in extended format: ["R"][n]["/"][duration]["/"][dateX]["T"][timeX].
A recurring time interval with start and duration in basic format: ["R"][n]["/"][date]["T"][time]["/"][duration].
A recurring time interval with start and duration in extended format: ["R"][n]["/"][dateX]["T"][timeX]["/"][duration].

A recurring time interval with start and end in basic format prefixes the interval with a recurrence marker: ["R"][n]["/"][date]["T"][time]["/"][date]["T"][time]. The recurrence count [n] may be omitted for unbounded repetition.
A recurring time interval with start and end in extended format prefixes the interval with a recurrence marker: ["R"][n]["/"][dateX]["T"][timeX]["/"][dateX]["T"][timeX].
When no recurrence count is provided, occurrences continue without bound. The designator ["R"] is immediately followed by a solidus ["/"].

requirements.category: Recurring time intervals with repeat rules
requirements.statement: The eligibility part determines frequency and duration using the F designator: ["F"][eligible-time-intervals].

requirements.category: Recurring time intervals with repeat rules
requirements.statement: Evaluating a repeat rule identifies eligible time intervals, applies selection rules, and derives the resulting occurrences.

requirements.category: Recurring time intervals with repeat rules
requirements.statement: Selection rules inherit values of lower-order time scale units from the time interval start, for units not specified in the eligibility part.

requirements.category: Recurring time intervals with repeat rules
requirements.statement: A recurring time interval with repeat rules consists of an optional occurrence count, a time interval, and a repeat rule.

requirements.category: Recurring time intervals with repeat rules
requirements.statement: Resulting occurrences carry a time scale unit resolution matching the lowest-order unit specified in the repeat rule.

requirements.category: Recurring time intervals with repeat rules
requirements.statement: A repeat rule combines an eligibility part (mandatory) and a selection part (optional): [eligibility-part][selection-part].

requirements.category: Recurring time intervals with repeat rules
requirements.statement: A recurring time interval with repeat rules combines the recurrence designator, count, interval, and repeat rule: ["R"][!][i]["/"][time-interval]["/"][repeat-rule].

requirements.category: Recurring time intervals with repeat rules
requirements.statement: The selection part provides matching conditions for instants within the eligible time intervals.
Only extended format representations shall be used. Basic format representations (without hyphens or colons as delimiters) are not permitted.
Date representations shall be complete calendar dates (YYYY-MM-DD) only. Reduced precision forms (YYYY or YYYY-MM) are not permitted as standalone values.
The second value 60 is permitted to represent a positive leap second. When a leap second occurs, the second field may contain the value "60" in place of the normal maximum of "59".
The UTC designator "Z" may alternatively be lowercase "z". Applications that generate this format SHOULD use uppercase "Z". Parsers SHALL accept both uppercase "Z" and lowercase "z".
The hour value 24 is not allowed. Midnight shall be represented as 00:00:00 of the following day.
Numeric UTC offsets shall include both hours and minutes (±hh:mm). Offset representations without minutes (±hh) are not permitted.

Time representations shall include seconds (hh:mm:ss). Fractional seconds (hh:mm:ss.s) are optional but the integer seconds field is mandatory. Representations with only hours and minutes (hh:mm) are not permitted.

The time designator between the date and time components shall be "T" or "t". Applications that generate this format SHOULD use uppercase "T". Parsers SHALL accept both uppercase "T" and lowercase "t".

The UTC offset "-00:00" indicates that the date-time is in UTC but the local time zone relationship is unknown. This differs from "+00:00" which indicates UTC with a known zero offset. Both "-00:00" and "+00:00" are valid representations.
Every date-time representation shall include either the UTC designator "Z" (or "z") or a numeric UTC offset (±hh:mm). Representations without a UTC offset are not permitted.
Advanced sub-year grouping identifiers use values 25-28 (hemispheric seasons), 33-36 (quarters), 37-39 (quadrimesters), and 40-41 (semestrals).
A hemispheric season or division placed in the month position of a date: [year]["-"][ydivision].
A basic season placed in the month position of a date: [year]["-"][season].
The basic season identifiers use numeric values 21 (Spring), 22 (Summer), 23 (Autumn), and 24 (Winter), without location dependence.
An explicit sub-year grouping encodes the value with the A designator: [i]["A"], where [i] ranges from 21 to 41.
An implicit advanced sub-year grouping encodes the division value directly: [ydivision], using values 25 through 41.
An implicit basic sub-year grouping encodes the season value directly: [season], using values 21 through 24.
Selection rules may be applied to any date and time expression in explicit form, substituting time scale components with selection expressions.
Time scale components may follow a selection rule set to apply to every date and interval described by that selection.
Selection by calendar day of month uses the explicit day expression [dayE] with values 1 through 31 and -31 through -1.
Selection by hour uses the explicit hour expression [hourE] with values 0 through 23.
Selection by minute uses the explicit minute expression [minE] with values 0 through 59.
Selection by calendar month uses the explicit month expression [monthE] with values 1 through 12.
Selection by ordinal day of year uses [dayoE(m)] with values 1 through 366 and -366 through -1.
Position selection identifies the i-th occurrence using an integer with the I designator: [position]["I"].
A selection rule set is enclosed by L prefix and N suffix designators: ["L"][selection-rule-1]...[selection-rule-n]["N"].
Selection by second uses the explicit second expression [secE] with values 0 through 60.
A selection combined with a time interval appends a duration to the selection expression: [selection]["/"][duration].
Selection by calendar week uses the explicit week expression [weekE] with values 1 through 53 and -53 through -1.
Selection by day of week uses the explicit day-of-week expression [daykE] with values 1 through 7.
A selection expression may serve as the start or end of a time interval.
An enumeration set encloses comma-separated date-time expressions in curly braces: ["{"][expr1][","][expr2]...["}"].
Range expansion may be applied inside enumeration and single-element sets.
Set notations and range expansion may also be used with integer values in date and time selection expressions.
A range of dates on or after a given expression, inclusive: [expr][".."].
A range of dates on or before a given expression, inclusive: [".."][expr].
A range spanning all values between two expressions, inclusive: [expr1][".."][expr2].
The "on or before", "on or after", and "between" range notations may be freely combined within a single set.
A single-element choice set encloses comma-separated expressions in square brackets: ["["][expr1][","][expr2]...["]"].

requirements.category: Significant digits for time scale components
requirements.statement: A year in exponential form that also accepts significant digits is denoted as [year(p, e, s)].

requirements.category: Significant digits for time scale components
requirements.statement: A four-digit year with significant digits is denoted as [year(s)].

requirements.category: Significant digits for time scale components
requirements.statement: A year longer than four digits, expressed with a letter prefix and accepting significant digits, is denoted as [year(p, s)].

requirements.category: Significant digits for time scale components
requirements.statement: Significant digits are encoded as [value]["S"][precision], where [value] is an estimated integer and [precision] is the count of significant digits starting from the leftmost digit of [value].

requirements.category: Significant digits for time scale components
requirements.statement: Any time scale component that accepts unbounded integers or describes a duration may substitute the integer placeholder [i] with a significant-digits value [sig].
Local time of day in basic format encodes the time designator followed by hour, minute, and second as contiguous fields: ["T"][hour][min][sec].
A specific hour in basic format encodes the time designator followed by the hour value: ["T"][hour].
A specific hour and minute in basic format encodes the time designator followed by hour and minute: ["T"][hour][min].
The beginning of a calendar day (midnight, start of day) is encoded as T000000 in basic format or 00:00:00 in extended format, denoting the first instant where no time has elapsed.
In expressions containing only time of day (including UTC and offset variants), the time designator ["T"] may be omitted where no ambiguity would result.

The ending of a calendar day (midnight, end of day) is encoded as T240000 in basic format or 24:00:00 in extended format. The hour value 24 is valid only when representing the last instant of the day.
Local time of day in extended format encodes the time designator followed by hour, minute, and second with colon separators: ["T"][hour][":"][min][":"][sec].
A specific hour and minute in extended format encodes hour and minute with a colon separator: [hour][":"][min].

A decimal fraction may be appended to the hour component, separated by a decimal sign (period or comma) with at least one digit. When a fraction is present on the hour, minute and second components are omitted. Only basic format applies.

A decimal fraction may be appended to the minute component, separated by a decimal sign (period or comma) with at least one digit. When a fraction is present on the minute, the second component is omitted.

A decimal fraction may be appended to the second component, separated by a decimal sign (period or comma) with at least one digit. When a fraction is present on the second, no lower-order components appear.
Local time with UTC offset in basic format appends the shift after the time: [time][shift] or [time][shiftH], where shift is [±][hour][min] and shiftH is [±][hour].
Local time with UTC offset in extended format appends the shift after the time: [timeX][shiftX] or [timeX][shiftH], where shiftX is [±][hour][":"][min] and shiftH is [±][hour].

A time shift is represented in basic format as [±][hour][min] or [±][hour], and in extended format as [±][hour][":"][min] or ["Z"]. The UTC designator ["Z"] indicates no time shift from UTC. The time shift shall be positive if ahead of or equal to UTC, and negative if behind UTC.
UTC time is indicated by appending the UTC designator ["Z"] directly after the time expression, with no intervening space.
Unspecified digits may appear at any position within a calendar date representation, not limited to rightmost components.
The unspecified digit rules extend to any date and time expression, including time-of-day components.
In explicit forms, "X" replaces any single digit within a time scale component value to indicate that digit is unspecified.
In explicit forms, "X*" marks an entire time scale component value as unspecified.
In implicit forms, "X" replaces individual digits to mark them as unspecified. Replacing all digits of a component indicates the entire component is unspecified.
Reduced precision with unspecified calendar month in explicit form: [yearE]["X*M"].
Reduced precision with unspecified calendar month in implicit form: [year]["-"]["XX"].
One to four rightmost digits of the calendar year may be replaced with "X" to indicate those digits are unspecified.
A calendar date with all components unspecified in explicit form: ["X*Y"]["X*M"]["X*D"].
A calendar date with all components unspecified in implicit form: ["XXXX"]["-"]["XX"]["-"]["XX"].
A calendar date with unspecified day in explicit form: [yearE][monthE]["X*D"].
A calendar date with unspecified day in implicit form: [year]["-"][month]["-"]["XX"].
A calendar date with unspecified month and day in explicit form: [yearE]["X*M"]["X*D"].
A calendar date with unspecified month and day in implicit form: [year]["-"]["XX"]["-"]["XX"].
Only extended format representations shall be used. Basic format representations (without hyphens or colons as delimiters) are not permitted.
Year shall be represented as exactly four digits. Two-digit year representations are not permitted. This avoids the ambiguity of two-digit century representations.
Fractional seconds, when present, shall consist of a decimal point followed by one or more digits.
Hour values shall be in the range 00 through 23. The 12-hour notation with am/pm is not permitted.
Only the following six forms are permitted: YYYY, YYYY-MM, YYYY-MM-DD, YYYY-MM-DDThh:mmTZD, YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssTZD, YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.sTZD. No other forms are permitted.
The time designator between the date and time components shall be "T" (uppercase or lowercase).
When time is present, the time zone designator (TZD) shall be either "Z" (for UTC) or a numeric offset in the form ±hh:mm. Time representations without a time zone designator are not permitted.

The week calendar is based on an unbounded series of contiguous calendar weeks. Each calendar week has seven calendar days identified by ordinal number from 1 (Monday) through 7 (Sunday). The reference point assigns Saturday to 1 January 2000.
A complete week date in basic format encodes the year, week number (prefixed by W), and day of week: [year]["W"][week][dayk].
A week date with reduced precision (day of week omitted) in basic format encodes only year and week number: [year]["W"][week].
An expanded week date in basic format encodes a signed expanded year, week number, and day of week: [±][year(expanded)]["W"][week][dayk].
An expanded week date with reduced precision in basic format encodes a signed expanded year and week number: [±][year(expanded)]["W"][week].
An expanded week date in extended format encodes a signed expanded year, week number, and day of week with hyphen separators: [±][year(expanded)]["-"]["W"][week]["-"][dayk].
An expanded week date with reduced precision in extended format encodes a signed expanded year and week with hyphen separator: [±][year(expanded)]["-"]["W"][week].
A complete week date in extended format encodes the year, week number (prefixed by W), and day of week with hyphen separators: [year]["-"]["W"][week]["-"][dayk].
A week date with reduced precision (day of week omitted) in extended format encodes year and week with hyphen separator: [year]["-"]["W"][week].
The calendar week of year is identified by a two-digit ordinal number from '01' for the first calendar week through '52' or '53', depending on the number of calendar weeks in that calendar year.

Each Gregorian calendar year can be identified by a 4-digit ordinal number beginning with '0000' for year zero, through '9999'. The year number may be preceded by a minus sign to indicate a year preceding year zero.
